items.body: This guide helps you create a port-forward rule in either the router app or its browser-based admin page for Xfinity Gateway. Keep the provider name (Xfinity / Comcast) separate from the actual device where settings are changed.

bullets: Confirm the host Mac is the device that will receive the forward.
Keep the router login open so you can return to the forwarding page if the firmware hides advanced settings.
Have the host Mac's local IP ready: Unavailable on this Mac right now.
Common admin addresses for this guide: 10.0.0.1, http://10.0.0.1.
Verify you are configuring the ISP gateway itself and not a separate downstream router or mesh system.
Target device / internal IP: Unavailable on this Mac right now
Recommended protocol guidance: Forward TCP for Java. Add UDP only when Bedrock or Geyser is enabled.
Bedrock port: Not enabled (usually UDP, when Bedrock/Geyser is enabled)

items.title: Confirm you are using the Xfinity gateway itself
items.body: If you also have your own router or mesh system, the forwarding rule may belong there instead.

items.title: Open xFi or log in to 10.0.0.1
items.body: Use the Xfinity app first if that is how your gateway is managed. Otherwise try 10.0.0.1 in a browser.

items.title: Go to the forwarding area
items.body: Find the section for advanced network settings and port forwarding. Xfinity labels and availability can vary by gateway generation.

items.title: Select the host Mac and enter the port values
items.body: Choose the Mac running Minecraft Server Controller. Forward TCP for the Java port. If Bedrock is enabled, also forward UDP for the Bedrock port.

items.title: Save and test externally
items.body: Save the rule, then test from a different network. If you cannot find forwarding at all, you may be on a restricted or app-only gateway flow.

items.title: Common flow
items.body: Xfinity gateway menus vary across XB6, XB7, and XB8 hardware revisions.

items.title: Restrictions
items.body: If the app or gateway firmware hides forwarding, verify you are not in bridge mode and that another router is not actually doing routing.
If the rule still does not work after you save and test from another network, continue with the matching troubleshooting topics below instead of guessing.

notes: xfinity-step-4 declares referencedTokens [.javaPort, .bedrockPort, .bedrockEnabled] but its body text contains no {{...}} placeholder at all -- resolveText only substitutes a token whose literal placeholder is present in the text, so the referencedTokens metadata alone never triggers substitution or an unresolvedTokens entry. Only the shared prerequisites/value-summary sections (which do contain literal placeholders) appear in unresolvedTokens.
